General Information
Selection for admission to The University of Texas neuroscience graduate program is based on a student’s research experience, academic achievements, personal statement and letters of recommendation. Research experience is a particularly important part of the application. Because of the interdisciplinary nature of this neuroscience program, students with a background in biological, physical, computational and psychological sciences are equally appropriate for the program. The program does not have specific course requirements, although completion of basic science and math undergraduate coursework is encouraged.
The Interdisciplinary Neuroscience Program is committed to training neuroscientists from all backgrounds. The University of Texas and the Neuroscience Graduate Program offer competitive fellowships to outstanding students, and international applicants are eligible for some of these fellowships.
The neuroscience graduate program does not require GRE scores or accept them in the application submission.
The pool of applicants is extremely competitive, and the majority of those admitted far exceed the minimum requirements.
INP Recruitment: Feb 24-27, 2027
Applicants who are invited to interview will be contacted in December. Recruitment visits will include interviews with faculty, the opportunity to interact with current INP students, postdocs and faculty, and information about the UT campus and about living in the city of Austin.
